main_concerns.concern: Documentation-as-progress anti-pattern: The main claim ("a single HTML page CAN safely summarize...") is trivially true on its face — of course a page CAN summarize. The real question is whether creating this page advances RedCap's complete revival or becomes another documentation artifact in a commit history already dominated by contracts, maps, doctrines, and lifecycle records. Constraint 2 ("do not turn a human-facing diagram into completion evidence") flags a known risk but doesn't prevent it — the constraint acknowledges the pattern exists while the proposal provides no mechanism to prevent the page from being cited later as "philosophy documented, phase complete."

minimum_fixes.minimum_fix: Before building the HTML page: (1) Write a one-paragraph content specification listing exactly what sections the page will have and which evidence document maps to each section. (2) Define a crisp "done" condition — e.g., "the page is done when it has been reviewed once by a human and no factual errors against the source contracts were found." (3) Add a prominent, non-dismissible status banner at the top of the page stating "RedCap complete revival: NOT DONE" with a link to terminal-goals.json. (4) Bind the page to a specific implementation milestone — do not let it float as a standalone artifact.
